name: Volkov-Saito Precision VS-44 'Fenris'
description:
The VS-44 Fenris is a heavy assault rifle chambered in 8.6mm caseless, designed to bridge the gap between standard infantry rifles and crew-served weapons. At nearly five kilograms unloaded, the Fenris is too heavy for conventional patrol use but devastating in the hands of augmented operators with reinforced skeletal systems or powered exoframes. Its 8.6mm round delivers energy comparable to legacy .338 Lapua at half the range, shredding Level III armor and punching through light vehicle panels.

Volkov-Saito designed the weapon for operators who are themselves weapons platforms — individuals whose physical augmentation allows them to handle recoil and weight that would be punishing for baseline humans. The stock interfaces with common spinal-mount weapon stabilization systems, and the BCI link includes a recoil-prediction algorithm that pre-tensions the operator's augmented musculature milliseconds before each shot.

The Fenris is not subtle. Its muzzle report is thunderous, its muzzle flash is visible in daylight, and its terminal effects are gratuitously destructive. Volkov-Saito sells it as a force multiplier for augmented combatants who need to deliver crew-served firepower from a man-portable platform.
specifications:
caliber: 8.6mm caseless
effective_range: 700m
rate_of_fire: 450 rpm (cyclic)
magazine_capacity: 20 rounds
weight: 4.9 kg
tactical_use: The Fenris turns a single augmented operator into a fire support element. Its 8.6mm round penetrates cover that stops intermediate calibers, and the recoil-prediction system maintains accuracy through sustained fire that would be impossible for unaugmented shooters. In urban combat, a Fenris operator can suppress hardened positions and engage light vehicles without requiring dedicated anti-materiel weapons. The weapon's weight and recoil make it impractical for baseline human use.
cultural_context: The Fenris occupies an uncomfortable space in the augmentation debate. It is a weapon that requires augmentation to use effectively, making it a tool exclusively for the enhanced. This exclusivity appeals to augmented operators who view their modifications as competitive advantages, while baseline humans see it as another door closed by the augmentation gap. In some communities, carrying a Fenris is a statement: I am more than you.
story_hooks: A baseline human operator has been using a Fenris without augmentation, absorbing punishing recoil that is slowly destroying their shoulder and spine. They cannot afford the augmentations but need the weapon's firepower to survive.
A series of vehicle ambushes using Fenris rifles points to an augmented operator gone rogue — but the ballistic signatures suggest the same weapon is appearing in multiple cities simultaneously.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist assault rifle with exaggerated proportions — oversized receiver, prominent heat dissipation fins, and a barrel assembly that dominates the silhouette. The Fenris reads as industrial and purposeful, designed for augmented physiology rather than ergonomic compromise. Its profile suggests contained violence: squared shoulders, aggressive angles, no unnecessary curves.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length 1,090mm | Barrel length 510mm | Width across receiver 65mm | Receiver depth 85mm (accommodating BCI interface housing)
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty and demanding — 4.9kg of unforgiving mass that rewards augmented strength. Balanced slightly forward of the magazine well to account for muzzle-heavy barrel geometry. An unaugmented operator would experience significant fatigue; in augmented hands, weight becomes stabilizing authority.
physical_description.primary_material: Hardened steel receiver with titanium-alloy barrel assembly. Polymer furniture (lower receiver, handguard) is reinforced glass-fiber composite rated for sustained thermal stress.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with heat-anodized bronze accents on the barrel. Upper receiver shows service wear — micro-scratches and carbon scoring from sustained firing. Some panels exhibit deliberate stippling for grip enhancement.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary | Bronze/copper heat-dissipation accents | Matte black polymer grips | Small touches of signal-red on BCI interface connector
physical_description.grip_texture: Stippled polymer handguard with deeply textured palm swell — aggressive enough to bite through synthetic gloves. Magazine well features coarse checkering. Pistol grip wraps in rubberized synthetic with subtle grip grooves, designed for armored gauntlets.
distinctive_features: Oversized muzzle brake with pronounced recoil-compensation fins visible from the front
Chunky heat-sink assemblies running along the barrel — heavy-duty cooling for sustained fire
Pronounced spinal-mount interface block at the rear receiver (raised, reinforced tang with alignment pins)
Top-mounted rail system with proprietary Volkov-Saito quick-detach indexing — allows BCI harness attachment
Recessed magazine well with anti-tilt geometry for reliable feeding of heavy 8.6mm caseless rounds
Thermal witness marks (discoloration rings) on barrel and heat sinks from extended use
Small BCI circuit-board visible through a recessed red-tinted window on the left side of the receiver
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: VOLKOV-SAITO PRECISION stamped in sharp Cyrillic-Latin hybrid font along the left receiver wall | Model designation VS-44 FENRIS in white infill below the rail system | Serial number on lower receiver in small caps | Small Φ currency symbol (denoting expensive premium tier) embedded in the pistol grip cap
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but maintained. Operators who use the Fenris are professionals — the weapon shows carbon deposits and heat-stress patina rather than neglect. Occasional improvised repairs or modifications (tape wrapping on thermal areas, custom sling mounts) common among independent operators. Never pristine; always purpose-scarred.
